title: Universal Counterdiabatic Quantum Sensing
summary: One of the primary applications of quantum mechanics is leveraging coherence to make incredibly sensitive measurements. One way to push the boundary of this sensitivity even further is to initially prepare a system in an entangled state, though the fragility of these states limits their usefulness. In this work, we propose a new approach by which sensitivity comes during the preparation of an entangled state, rather than first preparing the state and then using it for sensing.
